The question skeptics ask“Okay, so what’s the catch? Battery drain? Gas mileage? Something they don’t tell you?”

We tell you the catch before you buy, not in week three

You can tell a lot about a company by what it admits. So here’s everything, before you spend a dollar:

  • Battery: the draw is very low. If the truck will sit parked five to seven days or more, unplug it and plug it back in when you drive again. That’s the one condition.
  • Fuel: cylinder switching exists to save a little fuel, so you may give some of that back. That’s the trade: all your cylinders and no more switching on the lifters.
  • It’s a disabler, not a delete. The lifters stay in the engine. It stops the switching that wears them.
  • Auto stop/start: it doesn’t turn it off. If that’s what you’re shopping for, this isn’t it.

No surprises in week three. A brand willing to show you its limits on day one is a brand you can believe about everything else.

Quick questions

Will it fit my truck?

FullForce fits 2007 to 2022 GM V6 and V8 trucks and SUVs, including Silverado, Sierra, Tahoe, Yukon and Suburban.

How long does it take to install?

About 30 seconds. It plugs into the OBD2 port under the dash. No tools and no wiring.

Will it drain my battery?

The draw is very low. If the truck will sit parked for five to seven days or more, unplug it and plug it back in when you’re driving again.

Does it work with remote start?

Yes. Starting the truck remotely isn’t a step you have to undo or redo.

What if it doesn’t work out?

You have 60 days to send it back for your money, and a lifetime warranty on the unit after that.

Will I lose gas mileage?

Cylinder switching exists to save a little fuel, so you may give some of that back. That’s the trade for keeping all your cylinders and taking the switching off your lifters.

Can I take it out later?

Yes. Pull it out of the port and the truck is back to stock. It doesn’t reprogram anything.
